task.description: Step 0.5 registry lookup + Step 1 diagnosis and sizing call for ISS-0429 (Process.sleep inside alert-hook delivery blocking the platform-wide Scheduler.Poller). Determine whether this can be fixed now with existing supervision primitives or must wait for ISS-0425's tree redesign, per the issue's own 'reconcile rather than inventing a placement' instruction. Diagnosis only -- no implementation, per ISSUE-FIXER's role.

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): No prior `resolved` issue matches this exact symptom. ISS-0224 (resolved, WF03-ISS0224-20260822) is the closest analog -- same hazard class ('a GenServer executing a callback processes no other message, so the pool's/poller's own mailbox is frozen') -- but a DIFFERENT process (SandboxPool, not Poller) and a different call site (provision_sandbox/0 inside handle_call, not an HTTP delivery retry loop inside a background tick). Not a recurrence of ISS-0224's own fix; it is the SAME architectural mistake made a second time in a different module, which is exactly what ISS-0429's own description already says. No severity change from this lookup.

STEP 1 (diagnosis, reproduced by reading the call chain directly, not from the issue's prose alone):

CALL CHAIN CONFIRMED BY READING EACH HOP: Letflow.Scheduler.Poller.handle_info(:tick, state) (poller.ex:100) iterates schemas synchronously (Enum.each, poller.ex:107) then calls maybe_run_alert_detection/3 (poller.ex:148, called at line 110) which, per schema, calls Alerts.build_context_and_detect/3 (alerts.ex:630) -> run_detection/2 -> do_run_detection/3 -> evaluate_*/N -> fire_hooks/4 (alerts.ex:412) -> Enum.each over hooks -> deliver_with_retry/4 (alerts.ex:479, first call at line 422). deliver_with_retry/4 is TAIL-RECURSIVE and calls Process.sleep(backoff_delay(attempt, policy)) at alerts.ex:517 on every non-terminal failure, then recurses at line 518 with attempt+1, up to policy.max_attempts (default 3, alerts.ex:92-95). All of this executes on the Poller's own GenServer process -- maybe_run_alert_detection has a try/rescue around the Alerts call (poller.ex:153-157) but that only catches raises; Process.sleep is not a raise, it blocks the calling process for real wall-clock time regardless of any rescue clause. Confirmed: the Poller's handle_info/2 clause literally cannot return, and therefore cannot process its own next :tick (scheduled via Process.send_after at poller.ex:207, itself only enqueued AFTER handle_info returns, at line 121) nor any other message, until every hook for every tenant schema in that tick's schemas list has either succeeded or exhausted its retries. Root cause is exactly as ISS-0429 states: retry/backoff is deliberately synchronous logic (backoff_delay/2's semantics are correct and must not change) that mistakenly runs on a shared, latency-critical, single-instance GenServer instead of on an isolated worker.

WHY NO EXISTING TEST CAUGHT IT: alerts.ex's own tests exercise fire_hooks/deliver_with_retry directly against a real or mocked HTTP endpoint that responds immediately (success or a single terminal failure) -- none drives a hook against a hung/slow endpoint while concurrently asserting the Poller's OWN mailbox stays responsive, because no test starts the real supervised Poller GenServer under test (application.ex:146's start_scheduler: false gate -- confirmed by reading that config comment -- deliberately keeps the Poller out of the supervision tree in test, and Letflow.Scheduler's own tests call poll_and_fire/1 directly, bypassing the GenServer entirely). The defect is therefore invisible to both alerts_test.exs (no Poller in the loop) and any Poller test (no slow-hook scenario). This is the same blind spot ISS-0224's own diagnosis flagged for SandboxPool ('every current caller uses a pool with at most one claim in flight ... becomes reachable the moment ...') -- here the trigger condition is just 'any hook endpoint is slow or unreachable,' which is not a load-test edge case but an ordinary production failure mode.

AT-MOST-ONCE / DEDUPE SEMANTICS THAT MUST BE PRESERVED (read in full, fire_hooks/4 and check_and_record_emission/4, alerts.ex:412-454): check_and_record_emission/4 runs and COMMITS its Repo.insert (on_conflict: :replace_all, conflict_target: [:hook_id, :trigger_key]) SYNCHRONOUSLY and BEFORE deliver_with_retry/4 is ever invoked (alerts.ex:417-422) -- the emission-dedupe row is written unconditionally on the first attempt at a given emitted_key, independent of whether delivery itself later succeeds, fails, or is relocated to run elsewhere. This means the dedupe/at-most-once invariant is ALREADY fully established by the time any relocation of deliver_with_retry/4 would take effect -- moving deliver_with_retry/4 (all of it, including its own retry loop) off the Poller process does not touch check_and_record_emission/4 at all and cannot change what the dedupe key protects. Ordering across hooks within one fire_hooks/4 call (Enum.each, alerts.ex:413) is likewise unaffected by relocating delivery, since check_and_record_emission/4 already runs per-hook, in order, before any delivery is dispatched.

SIZING CALL (per this run's explicit brief): (a) FIXABLE NOW with EXISTING supervision primitives, does NOT need to wait for ISS-0425.

1. ISS-0425 status confirmed NOT started: `find handoffs -iname '*0425*'` and `find lib/letflow/design -iname '*0425*'` both return nothing. ISS-0425 itself is `status: open`, unactioned, and is explicitly an ARCHITECTURAL proposal about the shape of the WHOLE application.ex tree (layering strategy, :rest_for_one, InstanceSupervisor ownership, restart-intensity policy) -- not a proposal about where alert-hook delivery specifically should live. Its own point (3) ('Task.Supervisor sprawl... worth one deliberate review pass; keeping all six with consolidated rationale is a defensible outcome') explicitly contemplates that the six existing domain-scoped Task.Supervisors may legitimately stay as-is, i.e. adding a seventh does not presuppose or foreclose any particular resolution of ISS-0425.

2. application.ex's existing pattern (read in full) is: EVERY prior instance of 'isolate a background operation from a GenServer that must stay responsive' in this codebase was solved by adding ONE MORE dedicated, domain-named `Task.Supervisor` child to the existing flat list (SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor for ISS-0224, Engine.PluginTaskSupervisor, Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor, Engine.Wasm.ModuleRegistryTaskSupervisor, Engine.Wasm.CapabilityGateTaskSupervisor, Engine.Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistryTaskSupervisor) -- each with an inline comment explaining why it is NOT shared with the others (e.g. Wasm.ModuleRegistryTaskSupervisor's comment: 'module registration ... is an independent concern' from Lua/Plugin). This is additive to the child list, not a restructuring of :one_for_one/:rest_for_one strategy or intensity -- exactly the kind of change ISS-0425 itself does not need to have landed first. A new `Letflow.Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor` (or similarly named) child follows this precedent directly.

3. SandboxPool prior art (ISS-0224, read lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex in full) used `Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/3` PLUS a `handle_info({ref, result}, state)` clause because that fix needed to carry mutable pool-slot bookkeeping across the async boundary and reply to a parked `from`. Alert-hook delivery has NO analogous need: fire_hooks/4's caller (the Poller, transitively) never inspects deliver_with_retry/4's return value today (alerts.ex:422's call site discards it; run_detection/2's own @spec return type is `:ok` regardless), and deliver_with_retry/4's only externally-visible effect on exhaustion is a `Logger.error` call (alerts.ex:504-513) -- no DLQ row (explicitly disclaimed in the moduledoc, lines 23-29), no state written back that the Poller or anything else reads. This means delivery can be dispatched as a fully DETACHED, fire-and-forget task with NO owning GenServer state and NO `handle_info` correlation needed on the Poller side -- simpler than SandboxPool's shape, not more complex, because there is nothing to reply to and nothing to reconcile on completion.

4. CONCLUSION: the correct, minimal, semantics-preserving relocation is: fire_hooks/4's call to `deliver_with_retry(hook, payload, trigger_key, 1)` (alerts.ex:422) moves from a direct synchronous call to a `Task.Supervisor.start_child/2` (or `Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2` if a design wants the task monitored-but-uncollected) dispatch against a NEW dedicated `Task.Supervisor` added to application.ex's children list, placed with the same 'no ordering dependency' note the Lua/Wasm ones carry (nothing else depends on this supervisor's start order; unlike SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor it need not precede anything). `check_and_record_emission/4` stays exactly where it is, called synchronously from `fire_hooks/4` on the Poller's own process, BEFORE the Task is dispatched -- this is what preserves at-most-once/dedupe semantics unchanged. `backoff_delay/2` and `RetryPolicy` are untouched; the entire `deliver_with_retry/4` function body (including its own recursive `Process.sleep`) can run VERBATIM inside the spawned Task -- the sleep is no longer a defect once it is no longer occupying the Poller (or any other shared/latency-critical process). This is additive-only to application.ex and does not presuppose any ISS-0425 outcome (layering, :rest_for_one, restart intensity, or Task.Supervisor consolidation) -- if ISS-0425 later consolidates Task.Supervisors, this new one folds into that later, unforced.

WHY THIS DIAGNOSIS ROUTES TO CODE-DESIGNER RATHER THAN BEING IMPLEMENTED IN THIS STEP: ISSUE-FIXER's own role is diagnosis-only per WF-03 Step 1 and this agent's own Forbidden clause ('Do not implement the fix yourself... diagnosing and fixing in the same step removes the design gate this pipeline depends on') -- that constraint is unconditional and is not something a task-specific prompt can waive. The sizing call above (conclusion 'a' -- fixable now) answers the routing question this run was launched to answer; the exact Task.Supervisor name/placement, whether to use start_child vs async_nolink, whether to add a max_children or crash-isolation cap, and how to phrase the new child's application.ex comment (matching the existing six) are process-shape decisions this project routes through CODE-DESIGNER + CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR precisely because OTP supervision integrity is REVIEWER's named hard-gate concern -- an ISSUE-FIXER-authored supervision change would skip that gate.

OUT OF SCOPE, NOTED NOT SILENTLY DROPPED: lib/letflow/webhooks.ex:345's `deliver/3` (Letflow.Webhooks) has the identical Process.sleep-in-retry-loop shape but is confirmed CURRENTLY LATENT -- `grep -rn 'Webhooks.deliver(' lib/` outside webhooks.ex itself returns no production caller, only moduledoc mentions in webhooks/delivery.ex -- so it blocks nothing today. ISS-0429's own text scopes it out of this fix explicitly; this diagnosis does not touch it and it remains a still-open follow-up for whoever wires up REQ-183's dispatcher, exactly as the issue says.

WHAT A FIX DESIGN MUST COVER: (1) new `Task.Supervisor` child name + application.ex placement + comment matching the existing six's convention; (2) exact dispatch call at alerts.ex:422 (start_child+ignore vs async_nolink+deliberately-uncollected result) and whether `deliver_with_retry/4`'s @spec / call signature needs to change now that its caller no longer needs its return value; (3) crash isolation -- confirm an httpc timeout/exception inside the spawned Task cannot propagate back to fire_hooks/4's caller (it can't, by Task.Supervisor design, but the design doc should say so explicitly per REVIEWER's checklist); (4) a design note stating explicitly that `check_and_record_emission/4` remains synchronous and unchanged, and that `backoff_delay/2`/`RetryPolicy` values are unchanged, so CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR can confirm the 'no semantics change' constraint by inspection; (5) explicit non-scope note for webhooks.ex's latent instance, matching this diagnosis.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER (WF-03 Step 2) for fix design: relocate alerts.ex fire_hooks/4's deliver_with_retry/4 dispatch off the Poller process onto a new dedicated Task.Supervisor child in application.ex, per this diagnosis's conclusion. Sizing call: (a) fixable now with existing supervision primitives -- does not need to wait for ISS-0425.
